drafted_from: tool:make-a-vector-set-from-picture-vectors-my-apps-kept's own row and meaning/test/kept_vectors_check.py, whose run on a made-up asset index answered the values shown here
start_here: Say to your AI: "Turn the picture vectors in my asset index ~/Library/clip-index into vector sets in ~/picture-sets." It runs the converter on this computer and answers each set it made with its item count.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it only reads the stores you name and writes vector set folders on this computer.
instructions: 1. Name the store your program kept (an asset index, a folder of timed frames or a results store) and the folder for the sets.

2. Your AI reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:make-a-vector-set-from-picture-vectors-my-apps-kept"} and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/search-everything-with-one-question/meaning/do-work/make_vector_set_from_kept_vectors.py --asset-index {input} --out {output}.
3. Read the last line {"result": {"sets", "out"}}: each set folder holds items.jsonl, vectors.npy and vector-set.json for the index descriptor.
4. Search a set by words through tool:words-as-picture-vector, which makes vectors the same model compares.

worked_examples.title: An asset index becomes a video set and an image set
worked_examples.ask: Make my app's kept picture vectors searchable.
worked_examples.given: From meaning/test/kept_vectors_check.py: a made-up asset index with two video frames and one image.
worked_examples.hands_back: It printed result.sets {"asset-index-video": 2, "asset-index-image": 1}, and asset-index-video/vector-set.json says search_mode "exact".
